the_read: Three pre-launch and just-launched titles are doing more attention per dollar than the rest of the universe combined this week. Forza Horizon 6 at 57K live Twitch viewers three days pre-launch with 3.3M wishlists is the rare cross-platform AAA where Game Pass cannibalisation is the only binding question. Subnautica 2 held its 3.2M wishlists through EA launch without the sequel-disappointment decay — the rarer wishlist-discipline signal. And Slay the Spire 2 has booked $129M in 70 days without a publisher; the mixed reviews are a sign of engagement, not failure. Three different breakout shapes, same week.

And Slay the Spire 2 has booked $129M in 70 days without a publisher; the mixed reviews are a sign of engagement, not failure. Three different breakout shapes, same week.
the_read_by_cadence.weekly: The weekly filter cuts the daily noise: the universe right now is rich with first-of-publisher and pivot bets. Pocketpair Publishing's Windrose ($46M revenue, 1.95M owners in 30 days) is the proof-of-concept for a structural play — a small-studio publishing line capturing the niche nobody has institutionalised. Shiro Games' Farever pivots a grand-strategy studio into action-RPG (contested loop, engaged cohort). Mega Crit shipping StS 2 alone is the cleanest "no publisher needed" case on file. The pattern beneath the noise: small developer/publisher dyads continue to capture more breakout share than mid-tier publishers, and 2026 is when this becomes the consensus read.
the_read_by_cadence.monthly: The month's structural read is that wishlist counts above 3M are no longer rare. Forza Horizon 6, Subnautica 2, GTA VI, Hogwarts Legacy at its pre-launch peak — all four crossed the threshold. The 3M-wishlist bar used to be once-a-year; it's now four times per year and counting. That changes pre-launch marketing economics: wishlist accumulation as a one-time playable-demo-fed campaign is being replaced by multi-year drip-cohort accumulation. Studios who can't run that long campaign are at a structural disadvantage. The corollary: the highest-EV pre-launch indicator is no longer wishlist count, it's wishlist persistence — does the count hold through delay announcements, sequel reveals, content gaps. That's the new diagnostic.

the_read: Slay the Spire 2 is the highest-revenue EA launch on file: $129M booked in 70 days. Mega Crit shipped without a publisher and kept every dollar.

63% positive on 158K reviews is conspicuously mixed for the genre-defining studio. Cohort split is between original-StS purists complaining about deviations and new-cohort players. The next two patches resolve it either direction.
Steam owners cleared 6.8M units in 70 days at $25 SRP. This is what happens when the original's audience converts on a sequel with zero marketing budget.
thesis.against_consensus: Industry press hand-wringing about mixed reviews is misreading the signal. 6.8M units in 10 weeks with 158K reviews is the kind of engagement curve publishers spend a hundred million to manufacture. Reviews are mixed because lots of people are playing, not because the product is failing.
thesis.comparable: Original Slay the Spire's EA run captured ~250K reviews over 18 months. StS 2 hit 158K in 10 weeks — roughly 12× the review velocity. Projects to a long-tail outcome comparable to the original's ~$200M lifetime, with upside if Mega Crit nails the patch cadence.
thesis.what_would_change_my_mind: Two more weeks of declining concurrent + reviews going net-negative. Currently the velocity says the cohort is engaged, not disengaged.
risks: Sequel-purity backlash is the operational risk; patch cadence is the lever.
Roguelike-deckbuilder cluster is now saturated with imitators.
thesis.pull_quote: $129M booked in 70 days with no publisher. Mixed reviews are engagement, not failure.

the_read: Forza Horizon 6 is launching with 3.33M wishlists — that's a top-3 wishlist conversion event of the era, behind only Hogwarts Legacy and BG3.
57,000 concurrent Twitch viewers three days before launch with 96 streams running is pre-launch broadcast saturation. Xbox marketing got their money's worth from the streamer outreach.

Playground Games + Xbox Game Studios + 224K followers means the launch number is bounded only by Steam infrastructure. The interesting commercial question is the long-tail attach rate to Game Pass — every Game Pass subscriber who plays this is one less Steam purchase.
thesis.against_consensus: Consensus treats this as a guaranteed phenom-tier launch. Look closer: the post-Forza-5 retention curve was flatter than the franchise's prior median, and the audience that bounced on FH5 hasn't been re-recruited yet. Phenom on day-one peak, but the cohort settle is the real question.
thesis.comparable: Forza Horizon 5 at launch ran 71K peak CCU on Steam at a moment with lower wishlist counts. FH6's 3.3M wishlists are roughly 1.6× higher — projects to 110-130K Steam peak CCU if conversion holds, or 70-80K if Game Pass cannibalises Steam more heavily than FH5.
thesis.what_would_change_my_mind: A weekend-1 Steam peak below 60K would signal Game Pass cannibalisation is steeper than projected and the franchise plateau is real.
risks: Game Pass overlap caps Steam-side commercial upside.
Franchise plateau risk from FH5 retention shape.

the_read: Crimson Desert is at week 8 post-launch with $30M+ revenue tracking and signal compression. The Korean MMO-team-makes-action-game pivot delivered an actual cohort.
Pearl Abyss took 9 years to ship this from announcement. The launch curve is the patient-capital benchmark — most studios couldn't sustain that runway.
73% positive on 18K reviews with persistent Twitch presence post-launch is the second-wave-eligible shape. The interesting commercial question is the China-region rollout cadence.
thesis.against_consensus: Consensus over-discounted Crimson Desert because of the 9-year dev cycle. The launch performance shows that long-runway development is still viable for studios with prior cash buffer. The structural lesson is harder to extract than the SKU outcome.
thesis.comparable: Black Desert at week 8 post-launch (the predecessor): similar review velocity, slightly higher CCU floor. Crimson Desert is tracking ~80% of BDO's curve at the same window — predictable, not surprising.
thesis.what_would_change_my_mind: A 30-day decline in Korean-region CCU. Pearl Abyss's commercial model is more dependent on Asia rollout than Western markets.
risks: 9-year dev cycle was operationally expensive — payback period is the analyst question.
